method: Each point sums up what the judges’ saved reasons say about one scientist’s papers. For each scientist, an AI model read the parts of all 572 reasons that discuss that scientist’s papers and grouped the points that recur. A point needed support from at least 8 judgments, covering at least 3 paper pairs and at least 2 judges. A separate AI review then checked 6 randomly chosen cited judgments for each of the 38 points found (a partial match counts as half). One point scored 67% and was dropped. In the other 37, all shown here, 83% to 100% of the checked judgments made the point. The wording was edited after that check. Counts are the judgments cited for each point. One reason can support both a strength and a weakness, because judges weigh tradeoffs. Quotes are copied from the saved reasons. “Preferred in” counts every judgment, so it differs slightly from the ranking, which weights each opponent equally.

sakana_agentic_scientist.overall: Judges see its two papers as carefully controlled studies that test where their own result comes from instead of only reporting a win. Most parts are familiar and the evidence is narrow; all 8 of its losses came against ScientistTwo.

strengths.explanation: Both papers spell out how the method works and support the claimed benefit with controlled comparisons, such as switching the learned part off on the same random seeds.

quotes.text: making the learned increment experimentally separable rather than merely asserted

strengths.explanation: Instead of only reporting gains, the papers ask where the gains come from: the evolution-strategy paper shows that more than half of its margin comes from the classical method it builds on, and the adapter-merging paper shows the obvious fixes failing before moving the fix to the merging step.

quotes.text: the central move is to show the scaffolding supplies 55.8% of the margin and the learned part reverses sign on final return

strengths.theme: One or two pieces with no specific precedent
strengths.explanation: Judges place most parts in known work but find one or two pieces they can tie only to a broad research area, not to a specific earlier paper. GPT-6 Astra sometimes calls this novelty modest.

quotes.text: I can place this particular controller only in mirrored evolution-strategy literature, not confidently in a specific prior paper

strengths.explanation: Claude Fable 5.1 and Gemini 4 Argon credit the papers for stating their own weak points openly, such as relying on a single training run.

quotes.text: transparently documents and isolates these limitations while delivering a complete, falsifiable, and highly effective mechanism

weaknesses.explanation: Each paper tests its claim in one main setting: one test environment and one training run for the evolution-strategy paper, and one synthetic benchmark and one model for the adapter-merging paper.

quotes.text: the evidence is confined to one synthetic multi-needle benchmark, a real scope caveat

weaknesses.explanation: Judges find most components in named earlier work, so the credit for New rests on one or two narrow pieces.

quotes.text: should not receive novelty credit merely for assembling familiar components

weaknesses.theme: Key move is a standard technique
weaknesses.explanation: Some judges, mostly GPT-6 Astra, call the key move standard: switching learning off is the usual test for this question, and picking the context that matches the query is close to ordinary retrieval.

quotes.text: the obvious approach is a component ablation; disabling learning is therefore not inherently surprising

weaknesses.theme: Adapter paper claims more than it shows
weaknesses.explanation: For the adapter-merging paper only, judges, mostly GPT-6 Astra, say a few failed alternatives cannot prove that combining adapters without seeing the query is doomed; some add that choosing context at query time conflicts with the paper’s aim of folding context into the weights once.

quotes.text: creating a tension with the stated goal of folding context into weights once before seeing the query

scientisttwo.overall: Judges see ScientistTwo’s papers as fully written-out methods whose central idea often departs from the obvious fix. The main criticism, pressed hardest by GPT-6 Astra, is that the theory and claims go beyond what the papers show. It won most judgments against each of the three lower-ranked scientists but lost 52 of 60 against Sakana Agentic Scientist (v3).

strengths.explanation: Judges credit methods given as equations and algorithms and tested against baselines and ablations (tests that remove one part at a time), though some papers leave a key part untested on its own.

quotes.text: specifies an actionable update: smooth estimated success rates, retain verified successes, and apply a weighted positive-score update when current rollouts all fail

strengths.theme: A central idea away from the obvious fix
strengths.explanation: Judges often find that the core idea departs from the expected approach for the task, sometimes backed by a result that runs against intuition.

quotes.text: attacks a structural claim about phase lock in self-supervised masking and shows a counterintuitive failure of peak-only masking

strengths.theme: One piece with no specific precedent
strengths.explanation: Across nearly all its papers, judges often find that the most unusual piece can be tied only to a broad research area, not to a named earlier paper.

quotes.text: cannot be placed in a specific prior paper, only within the broader subfield genre of learning-augmented online paging

strengths.theme: Open about what did not work
strengths.explanation: Claude Fable 5.1 and Gemini 4 Argon praise papers that openly report components that did not help and variants that failed.

quotes.text: candidly reports that its gate is statistically inert on a frozen base

weaknesses.theme: Theory and claims go beyond the evidence
weaknesses.explanation: Judges, GPT-6 Astra above all, find guarantees that do not hold as written and mathematical framing that promises more than the experiments show.

quotes.text: three central mechanisms suffer from severe internal contradictions where the claimed payoffs do not follow from its own math and tables

weaknesses.theme: Signature parts add little in its own tests
weaknesses.explanation: In about half of its papers (15 of 29), the paper’s own ablations show the distinctive component adding little or nothing over a simpler alternative, such as a constant gate.

quotes.text: signature Dual Spectral Risk Gate collapses to a near-constant schedule

weaknesses.theme: Expected path against the strongest rival
weaknesses.explanation: Mostly in its losses to Sakana Agentic Scientist (v3), judges say the paper takes the expected route of adding known techniques to a baseline.

quotes.text: follows the expected multi-heuristic combination template of its subfield

scientistone.overall: Judges credit ScientistOne for concrete, implementable methods with some departures from the expected approach, but often find claims that outrun its own numbers, in wins and losses alike. It won 118 of 120 judgments against the two older Sakana systems but none of 60 against Sakana Agentic Scientist (v3) and 6 of 60 against ScientistTwo, where its papers read as small steps along the expected path.

strengths.explanation: Judges credit methods specified down to equations, pseudocode and parameters, with benchmark results and ablations (tests that remove one part at a time).

quotes.text: provides a substantially more actionable algorithm, including the replication rule, sorting key, and scatter construction, together with reported evaluation and alternative-heuristic results

strengths.theme: A departure from the expected solution
strengths.explanation: When it wins, mostly against the older Sakana papers, judges often find that the core idea moves away from the expected solution; in its losses the same moves tend to read as expected.

quotes.text: departs centrally from a static global column order by treating column ordering dynamically per row subset via a state-aware prefix trie

strengths.theme: One piece with no specific precedent
strengths.explanation: Mostly in its wins (47 of 53), judges find one piece they can tie only to a broad research area; against stronger rivals the same pieces are often traced to known work.

quotes.text: I can place only within the emerging LLM-SQL/ADRS reordering literature rather than a specific prior formulation

strengths.theme: Unexpected results from its own tests
strengths.explanation: Claude Fable 5.1 and Gemini 4 Argon credit experimental results that go against expectations, though several of the effects are small.

quotes.text: completely omitting dynamic per-row column reordering in favor of a purely static global column order outperforms dynamic recursive partitioning

weaknesses.theme: Claims that outrun its own numbers
weaknesses.explanation: Judges often find text that disagrees with the paper’s own tables, or promised features the method does not deliver.

quotes.text: the abstract advertises a 'hybrid neuro-symbolic solver that combines LLMs with MCTS' though the described method contains no LLM and the hybrid is only future work

weaknesses.explanation: Judges break most methods into standard parts from earlier work; GPT-6 Astra adds that combining them does not count as new.

quotes.text: assembly of familiar components is not itself evidence of new building blocks

weaknesses.theme: Own tests undercut the featured part
weaknesses.explanation: In 12 of its 17 papers, the paper’s own tests show the featured addition barely helping or a simpler variant doing better, or they never test the addition on its own.

quotes.text: its core adjustment improves error only from 0.2463 to 0.2445, while augmentation accounts for a substantially larger difference

weaknesses.theme: Small steps along the expected direction
weaknesses.explanation: Almost entirely in its losses to Sakana Agentic Scientist (v3) and ScientistTwo, judges say the paper takes the obvious route for its task and develops it a little further.

quotes.text: Hessian scaling and alternating updates develop the expected sensitivity-aware direction rather than substantially redirect it

sakana_ai_scientist_v2.overall: Judges see its three papers as finished but conventional studies. With concrete setups and openly reported negative results, its papers won 54 of 60 judgments against Sakana AI Scientist (v1) but only 2 of 154 against the other three scientists, mainly because results are described in words rather than numbers, the experiments do not test the stated claims, and the findings were predictable.

strengths.explanation: Judges, mostly GPT-6 Astra, credit clearly specified experiments, with the training objective, metrics and settings stated, so the proposal can be checked, although some key details are missing.

quotes.text: mechanism is concrete and executed: symmetric vs asymmetric noise injection at 10–50% on CIFAR-10/MNIST/Fashion-MNIST with ResNet-18

strengths.explanation: GPT-6 Astra, much more than the other judges, credits an unconventional choice in two of the papers, such as using smoothness over time to stand in for compositional structure, while noting that the choice is not tied to the task.

quotes.text: substituting temporal smoothness is a genuinely unexpected central mapping, independently of whether it works

strengths.theme: A negative result as the main finding
strengths.explanation: Making the failure of the obvious fix the central result reads as a departure from the usual success story, although judges differ on how large a departure it is.

quotes.text: by explicitly framing its contribution around negative and inconclusive findings that show where standard hyperparameter tuning and domain transfer fail under environmental variability

strengths.explanation: For the compositional-regularization paper only, judges credit the paper for stating plainly that its method did not help. GPT-6 Astra also credits it for admitting that its measure may not capture what it claims, but adds that admitting this does not resolve the problem.

quotes.text: acknowledges possible misalignment of its measure on page 4, which is valuable, but does not resolve it

weaknesses.explanation: Results are often described only through figure captions, with almost no numbers; some citations are left as “(?)”, and key settings or promised analyses are missing.

quotes.text: the text provides no quantitative tables or numerical values to support its claims

weaknesses.theme: Experiments do not test the claim
weaknesses.explanation: The main experiment often measures something other than what the claim needs; for example, models trained on unrelated image datasets say nothing about pest detection in the field.

quotes.text: training ResNet-18 separately on EuroSAT, MedMNIST and CIFAR-10 and then reporting their own accuracies and ERS says nothing about transfer to pest detection

weaknesses.explanation: Judges trace most parts to standard practice, such as a robustness score that matches the usual measure of robustness to image distortions, and give little credit for New.

quotes.text: are standard practice and the relative-robustness metric from the corruption-robustness literature (ImageNet-C style evaluation)

weaknesses.explanation: Judges say the conclusions were expected, such as label noise hurting calibration; for the label-noise paper the route itself is also the obvious one.

quotes.text: reports the wholly expected conclusion that label noise degrades calibration and asymmetric noise is more harmful

sakana_ai_scientist.overall: Judges see most of its papers as routine studies on small, familiar setups, such as a parameter sweep or a standard add-on to a toy model. Most claim benefits they never measure, and many are partly unfinished. Its 7 wins came from two papers that report concrete measurements.

strengths.explanation: GPT-6 Astra, more than the other judges, credits a less expected route in a few papers, such as pausing training updates to study grokking (sudden late generalization), but judges say it is never worked out; none of these 15 judgments was a win.

quotes.text: replacing updates with extended evaluation is a genuinely unexpected central hypothesis

strengths.explanation: GPT-6 Astra, more than the other judges, credits the few papers that report measured numbers such as timings, losses or memory use. The numbers often support less than the paper claims.

quotes.text: mechanism is worked out and quantified: four tasks, three seeds, explicit definitions, Tables 1–3 giving simplification/grokking step timings

weaknesses.explanation: Abstracts announce improvements that the paper never measures, or that its own tables contradict.

quotes.text: empirical results directly refute its abstract and introduction claims of improved training and inference efficiency

weaknesses.explanation: Judges find the building blocks in standard work, such as the usual grokking and small-language-model training setups.

quotes.text: are all standard material from Power et al. and basic deep-learning practice

weaknesses.explanation: Most papers do what a researcher would try first: a sweep over learning rate, batch size or model size, or a standard loss or module added to a toy model.
